tasks.short: Check and approve invoices, agency bills and payment batches above my limit before Rabobank pays them.

today.trigger: Supplier invoices, staffing agency invoices and expense claims land in the AFAS approval workflow; the weekly payment batch is ready for sign-off.
steps: Open the invoices waiting for controller approval in AFAS Profit
Check each against the purchase order, contract or agency hours in the agency portal
Chase budget holders on Teams or Outlook for missing approvals or cost centres
Approve or reject in AFAS and note the reason
Review and sign the payment batch in Rabobank internet banking
drudgery: Matching agency invoice lines to hours worked per flex worker, site and week
Re-checking IBAN changes and duplicate invoices by hand
today.time_sinks: Agency invoices from three agencies with different layouts and hourly rate tables, which swing with the season (150 to 300 flex workers).

lenses.faster: Invoices that match PO, contract rate and agency hours arrive pre-checked with a green flag, so the controller only reads the exceptions instead of every line.
lenses.autonomous: Each new invoice in AFAS triggers a check against policy, approval matrix, PO and agency hours; clean ones under the threshold go straight to the batch.
lenses.ambitious: Every agency invoice checked line by line against CAO rates, shift allowances and actual clock hours, recovering overbilling that today slips through.
lenses.joy: No more scrolling through agency PDFs; the controller keeps the judgement calls on odd spend and new suppliers.
lenses.options: For a disputed agency invoice, the system proposes pay in full, short-pay with credit note request, or hold, with the euro effect of each.
lenses.altitude: The controller owns the approval matrix and matching rules and reviews a monthly report of what was auto-approved and why.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer supplier dispute follow-up
HR Administrator check of flex worker hours

tasks.human_edge: Saying no to a manager's spend, judging unusual or first-time payments, and signing the bank batch as the person accountable under the four-eyes rule.
tasks.pattern_why: Several sources (AFAS, agency portals, contracts) and messy exceptions; the match itself is rule-based but the agency invoices need extraction, and payment release must stay with a person.

in_practice.trigger: Invoice registered in AFAS Profit or agency invoice received by e-mail.
steps: Extract invoice lines and match to PO, contract rates and agency hours
Apply approval matrix and fraud checks (IBAN change, duplicate, new supplier)
Route clean invoices under threshold to the batch; flag exceptions with a short reason
Controller approves exceptions and signs the Rabobank batch
in_practice.human_gate: Controller approves every flagged invoice and every payment batch; bank release keeps two signatures.
data_needed: Agency rate cards per CAO function group
Hours per flex worker from agency portals
Open POs and supplier master data
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS Profit workflow history plus an exception log in SharePoint for the auditor

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit has configurable workflows for invoice approval with mandate limits.
LLMs can extract line items from varied invoice layouts reliably enough for matching with human review of mismatches.

risks: Payment fraud through changed supplier IBANs if checks are trusted blindly
Auto-approval drifting past mandate limits if the matrix is not maintained
Auditor rejects the control if the log is not complete
research_questions: What share of last quarter's invoices would have matched PO and rates without any touch?
Do the three agency portals export hours per worker in a usable format or only PDF?
How much overbilling did a manual sample of agency invoices find last year?
Will the external auditor accept rule-based auto-approval under a threshold as a key control?

tasks.short: Watch cash position, bank covenants and tax and premium payment deadlines so we never breach or pay late.

today.trigger: Daily morning check, plus month end and VAT and payroll tax deadlines.
steps: Download Rabobank statements and update the cash sheet in Excel
Compare against expected receipts and planned payments
Check headroom on the credit facility and covenant ratios
Track due dates for BTW, loonheffingen and pension premiums
Report cash position to the Finance Director
drudgery: Copying bank balances into Excel every morning
Rebuilding the covenant calculation each quarter
Keeping a calendar of tax and premium deadlines by hand
today.time_sinks: Reconciling expected customer receipts to actual bank lines when debtors pay late or in bulk.

lenses.faster: The daily cash sheet builds itself from the bank feed and AFAS, so the morning check takes minutes instead of most of an hour.
lenses.autonomous: A nightly job computes cash, 13-week outlook and covenant ratios and sends an alert only when a threshold or deadline is at risk.
lenses.ambitious: A rolling 13-week cash forecast the bank and the board trust, updated daily, with covenant headroom shown months ahead.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses copying bank balances; the controller spends the time on why cash moved.
lenses.options: Show cash under base, late-paying top-10 customers, and peak-season flex cost scenarios.
lenses.altitude: The controller designs the thresholds and the forecast logic and reviews forecast versus actual each month.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer DSO monitoring

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what to do when headroom gets tight and talking to the bank before a covenant problem becomes one.
tasks.pattern_why: Bank data, ledger data and covenant formulas are structured and the rules can be written down; no model is needed to run it.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly after the Rabobank statement import and the AFAS extract refresh.
steps: Import bank statements and AFAS open items
Compute cash position, 13-week outlook and covenant ratios
Check tax and premium deadlines against the payment plan
Publish to Power BI and alert by Teams on breaches
in_practice.human_gate: Controller reviews alerts and approves any action toward the bank or Belastingdienst.
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI dataset history and an alert log in SharePoint

evidence.claim: Rabobank offers statement exports in standard formats usable for automated import.
Cash forecasting tools such as Agicap build rolling cash forecasts from bank feeds.

risks: Wrong covenant definition coded once and trusted for months
Missed deadline if the tax calendar is not kept current
research_questions: Is the Rabobank feed available daily via API or only by manual download?
How far off was last year's cash forecast at four and twelve weeks?
Which covenant definitions in the facility agreement need judgement (adjustments) rather than a formula?

tasks.short: Decide when we need extra funding or lease finance, and where to park surplus cash.

today.trigger: Seasonal peaks, planned investments (trucks, forklifts, racking) and quarter-end cash review.
steps: Pull cash forecast and investment plan into Excel
Compare credit line, lease and own-cash options
Ask Rabobank and lease companies for quotes
Write a recommendation memo for the Finance Director
drudgery: Rebuilding the same lease-versus-buy model for each asset
Collecting and comparing quotes in different formats
today.time_sinks: Getting a reliable forecast of peak-season cash needs from operations.

lenses.faster: A standard model takes the cash forecast and quotes and produces the comparison in an hour instead of two days.
lenses.autonomous: When the 13-week forecast shows headroom below the set floor, a funding need note is drafted automatically.
lenses.ambitious: Every asset decision (trucks, forklifts, warehouse automation) gets a proper financing comparison, not just the big ones.
lenses.joy: Less spreadsheet rebuilding; more time negotiating terms.
lenses.options: Three to five financing routes side by side with cost, covenant effect and flexibility.
lenses.altitude: The controller sets the treasury policy (minimum cash, approved deposit types, lease rules) and the model applies it.

tasks.human_edge: Judgement on risk appetite, the bank relationship and timing.
tasks.pattern_why: The recommendation is a judgement for management; AI speeds the analysis and drafting.

in_practice.trigger: Forecast headroom alert or a planned investment above a threshold.
steps: Load forecast, quotes and policy into a standard Excel model
Copilot drafts scenario comparison and memo
Controller adjusts assumptions and writes the recommendation
in_practice.human_gate: Finance Director and board decide on any funding or deposit.

evidence.claim: Microsoft Copilot in Excel can build scenario tables and summarise models.

risks: Over-trust in a model that hides wrong interest or residual value assumptions
research_questions: How many financing decisions a year are made without a formal comparison?
Is there a written treasury policy the model can apply?
What did the last lease-versus-buy decision cost in time and was it right in hindsight?

tasks.short: Run the yearly budget and steer the finance team's planning and procurement work.

today.trigger: Annual budget cycle from September, quarterly reforecasts, team planning.
steps: Send budget templates to site and department managers
Chase and consolidate submissions in Excel
Review with FP&A, challenge assumptions with managers
Load the final budget into AFAS and Power BI
Plan and assign team work for close and audit
drudgery: Merging dozens of Excel files with changed layouts
today.time_sinks: Version chaos across budget files and repeated rounds with site managers.

lenses.faster: Budget inputs come in through one structured form, so consolidation is instant and rounds focus on the numbers that changed.
lenses.autonomous: Reminders and status per manager go out automatically; the consolidated draft refreshes as inputs arrive.
lenses.ambitious: Driver-based budgets per site (volume, shifts, flex share, CAO raises) instead of last year plus a percentage.
lenses.joy: No more file merging; the conversations with site managers stay.
lenses.options: Budget versions for low, base and high volume seasons, with flex worker cost per scenario.
lenses.altitude: The controller designs the budget model and drivers; FP&A and site managers run it.
reach: HR Business Partner headcount planning input

tasks.human_edge: Negotiating targets with site managers and keeping the team aligned.
tasks.pattern_why: Directing people and negotiating budgets stays human; AI handles consolidation, reminders and variance drafting.

steps: Send structured input forms per cost centre
Auto-consolidate and flag outliers versus drivers and last year
Draft challenge questions per manager
Controller holds review meetings and locks the budget
in_practice.human_gate: Controller and Finance Director sign off each budget version.
data_needed: Volume and shift drivers per site

evidence.claim: Copilot in Excel and Teams can summarise submissions and draft follow-up messages.

risks: Managers disengage if the budget feels machine-made
research_questions: How many hours go into consolidation versus review in the current cycle?
Are volume and shift drivers available per site from operations systems?
Would site managers use a structured form instead of Excel?

tasks.short: Advise the Finance Director and management team on financial goals, policies and big decisions.

today.trigger: Monthly MT meeting, ad hoc questions on pricing, sites, contracts or investments.
steps: Gather numbers from AFAS and Power BI
Build analysis in Excel
Write a short memo or slides
Discuss in the MT meeting
drudgery: Pulling the same figures for each new question
today.time_sinks: One-off analyses that start from scratch each time.

lenses.faster: A copilot answers 'what does this do to margin' questions from the ledger in minutes and drafts the memo.
lenses.autonomous: A monthly briefing on margin per customer and site is drafted after close without being asked.
lenses.ambitious: Every commercial decision (tender, rate increase, new site) gets a quick financial check before it is made.
lenses.joy: Less formatting, more discussion with the MT.
lenses.options: Present three policy options with effects rather than one recommendation.
lenses.altitude: The controller curates the data model and the standard analyses that management can query themselves.

tasks.human_edge: Trust, context about people and the business, and the courage to give unwelcome advice.
tasks.pattern_why: Advice depends on trust and judgement; AI prepares numbers and drafts.

in_practice.trigger: Question from MT or month-end close.
steps: Copilot pulls figures from the Power BI model
Drafts analysis and options
Controller checks and edits
Controller presents and advises
in_practice.human_gate: Controller owns every piece of advice given.

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI can answer natural-language questions on a semantic model.

risks: Wrong numbers from a poorly defined semantic model
Advice that sounds confident but misses context
research_questions: Which MT questions recur and could become standard analyses?
Is the Power BI model clean enough for natural-language queries?
Does margin per customer exist at all today?

tasks.short: Manage insurance and benefit costs: pension, absence insurance, eigenrisicodrager, and budget the premiums.

today.trigger: Annual renewals, premium notices from the pension fund and UWV, law changes, budget cycle.
steps: Collect premium notices and policy terms
Check rules changes (Wet toekomst pensioenen, Ziektewet and WGA premiums)
Budget premiums per site in Excel
Discuss renewals with broker and HR
Book and reconcile premiums in AFAS
drudgery: Reading premium letters and regulatory updates
today.time_sinks: Working out the cost effect of being eigenrisicodrager for ZW and WGA with absence data.

lenses.faster: An assistant summarises regulatory changes and policy documents and pre-fills the premium budget.
lenses.autonomous: Premium invoices are matched to AFAS headcount and payroll each month, with differences flagged.
lenses.ambitious: An annual review of eigenrisicodrager versus public insurance with real absence data, done properly every year.
lenses.joy: No more reading every circular; the broker discussion keeps the substance.
lenses.options: Cost scenarios for insurance choices and pension transition paths.
lenses.altitude: The controller sets the benefit cost model with the Compensation and Benefits Specialist and checks its outputs.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist premium reconciliation
HR Business Partner absence cost insight under Wet verbetering poortwachter

tasks.human_edge: Choices with the broker, HR and the works council, which has a say on pension and some benefit changes.
tasks.pattern_why: Mixed documents and policy choices with HR and OR involvement; AI summarises and calculates.

in_practice.trigger: Premium notice, renewal date or regulatory change.
steps: Summarise the change and its cost effect
Reconcile premium invoices to payroll headcount
Draft budget lines and options
Controller decides with HR and broker
in_practice.human_gate: Controller and HR Director approve; OR consulted where required.
in_practice.logs_to: Benefits budget file and decision notes on SharePoint

evidence.claim: LLMs can summarise regulatory and policy documents for review.

risks: Use of individual absence data beyond what AVG allows
research_questions: Is Noordhaven eigenrisicodrager for ZW or WGA today?
Do premium invoices reconcile to payroll without manual work?
Which part of this task really sits with the Compensation and Benefits Specialist?

tasks.short: Check payroll deductions, tax and pension liabilities and reconcile the AFAS payroll journal to the ledger.

today.trigger: Each payroll run (monthly and four-weekly) and the monthly loonaangifte.
steps: Receive payroll journal from the Payroll Specialist
Reconcile wage tax, social premiums and pension deductions to the GL
Check the loonaangifte against the journal
Investigate differences and correct postings
drudgery: Tick-and-tie of payroll totals to ledger accounts
Hunting for small differences from corrections
today.time_sinks: Differences from retroactive corrections and mixed monthly and four-weekly periods.

lenses.faster: An automatic reconciliation shows only the differences, so the check takes minutes.
lenses.autonomous: After each payroll run, the reconciliation runs and posts a status; clean runs need no touch.
lenses.ambitious: Full reconciliation of every run and every liability account, not samples.
lenses.joy: No more ticking totals; only real differences are investigated.
lenses.options: Not much need for options; one correct answer.
lenses.altitude: The controller owns the reconciliation rules and the exception review.

tasks.human_edge: Judging and resolving real errors with payroll.
tasks.pattern_why: Structured data, fixed rules, checkable output.

steps: Pull payroll journal and GL balances
Match per component and period
Flag differences above tolerance
Controller resolves exceptions with payroll
in_practice.human_gate: Controller signs off the reconciliation each period.
in_practice.logs_to: Reconciliation file in SharePoint per period

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit holds payroll and ledger in one system, allowing automated reconciliation queries.

risks: Payroll personal data exposed in reconciliation files (AVG)
research_questions: How many hours per run go to reconciliation today?
What are the most common causes of differences?
Can AFAS GetConnectors provide the needed data?

tasks.short: Prepare the monthly management pack, forecasts, annual accounts and regulatory filings like VAT and CBS.

today.trigger: Month-end close, quarterly VAT, annual accounts and audit, CBS surveys.
steps: Close the ledger with accountants
Extract trial balance and build the pack in Excel and PowerPoint
Write variance commentary
Prepare VAT return and statistics
Review with Finance Director
today.time_sinks: Collecting explanations for variances from site managers.

lenses.faster: The pack builds from AFAS automatically and a first draft of variance commentary is ready on day 2.
lenses.autonomous: After close, the pack, the forecast update and a draft commentary are generated and routed for review.
lenses.ambitious: Close in four days with a forecast the business trusts, plus site-level packs every month.
lenses.joy: No copy-paste; the controller writes the story.
lenses.altitude: The controller designs the pack and the forecast model and reviews output.

tasks.human_edge: Interpreting results, signing off and standing behind numbers to the auditor and the board.
tasks.pattern_why: Many steps across ledger, dashboards and commentary; drafts must be reviewed before release.

steps: Refresh pack from AFAS data
Draft variance commentary from ledger detail
Ask site managers for missing explanations
Controller reviews and releases
in_practice.human_gate: Controller and Finance Director approve every pack and filing.

evidence.claim: Copilot in Excel and PowerPoint can draft summaries and slides from data.

risks: Filing errors if drafts are not checked
research_questions: How many days does close take now, and where do they go?
Which variance explanations repeat monthly?
What does the auditor require for review evidence?

role.altitude: From approving, reconciling and building packs to designing and owning the control and reporting system: approval rules, reconciliations, cash and covenant monitoring, and the pack, with the controller reviewing exceptions and giving advice.
reach: FP&A Analyst forecasting and scenario work
Credit and Collections Officer DSO monitoring
Compensation and Benefits Specialist premium reconciliation
role.ceiling_note: Signing authority, audit accountability, bank and works council relationships and management advice stay human; about 40 to 50 percent of hours on these tasks can be freed, mostly in approvals, reconciliations and reporting.
skills_to_grow: Designing controls for automated approval and reconciliation
Data protection (AVG) in finance data flows
role.ambitious_version: A four-day close with a rolling 13-week cash and 12-month forecast trusted by the board, every invoice checked, and the controller spending most time advising on margins per customer and site.
